comparisons.comparison: Bank of America’s sensitivity analysis, like JPMorgan’s, evaluates the potential impact to forecasted net interest income over the next 12 months from instantaneous parallel and non-parallel shocks to the forward curve. Both companies use these scenarios to estimate potential baseline changes driven by interest rate movements. However, BAC’s disclosure focuses on the presentation of spot and forward rates and the resulting pretax impact tables, whereas JPM’s disclosure provides more textual detail on the specific composition of the yield curve shifts (parallel, steepening, flattening) and the inclusion of balance sheet forecasts and deposit betas.

sentences.text: Earnings-at-risk scenarios estimate the potential change to a baseline over the following 12 months utilizing multiple assumptions.

These scenarios include a parallel shift involving changes to both short-term and long-term rates by an equal amount; a steeper yield curve involving holding short-term rates constant and increasing long-term rates; and a flatter yield curve involving increasing short-term rates and holding long-term rates constant or holding short-term rates constant and decreasing long-term rates.
Table 43 presents the spot and 12-month forward rates used in developing the forward curve used in our baseline forecasts at December 31, 2024 and 2023.

Table 44 shows the potential pretax impact to forecasted net interest income over the next 12 months from December 31, 2024 and 2023 resulting from instantaneous parallel and non-parallel shocks to the market-based forward curve.

comparisons.peer_topic: Interest Rate Exposure (IRE) Metrics and Methodology
comparisons.peer_summary: Citi measures Banking Book interest rate risk using Interest Rate Exposure (IRE), which analyzes scenario impacts on net interest income against a base case using static balance sheet assumptions, market-implied forward rates, and specific flooring assumptions.
comparisons.comparison: Citi’s Interest Rate Exposure (IRE) analysis and JPM’s Earnings-at-Risk both estimate potential changes to baseline net interest income over 12 months using scenario assumptions that include instantaneous rate impacts, balance sheet forecasts, prepayment/reinvestment behavior, and deposit betas. Both explicitly assume no risk-mitigating actions by management in response to the rate changes. JPM details specific curve shapes (parallel, steepening, flattening), while Citi describes its methodology generally as analyzing scenario impacts against a base case.

sentences.text: Earnings-at-risk scenarios estimate the potential change to a baseline over the following 12 months utilizing multiple assumptions.
• The impact on exposures as a result of instantaneous changes in interest rates from baseline rates.
Citi utilizes the most recent quarter-end balance sheet, assuming no changes to its composition and size over the forecasted horizon (holding the balance sheet static).
The forecasts incorporate expectations and assumptions of deposit pricing, loan spreads and mortgage prepayment behavior implied by the interest rate curves in each scenario.
The forecasts do not assume Citi takes any risk-mitigating actions in response to changes in the interest rate environment.
Deposit pricing sensitivities (i.e., deposit betas) are informed by historical and expected behavior.

comparisons.peer_summary: Corporate Treasury measures EaR over a one-year horizon following 100- and 200-basis point instantaneous parallel shocks in interest rates relative to a baseline scenario. Models incorporate contractual elements, balance sheet composition assumptions, prepayment behavior, and deposit repricing calibrated using historical behavior and competitive landscape, with continuous monitoring of key assumptions.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs describe Earnings-at-Risk (EaR) scenarios based on instantaneous parallel shifts in interest rates over a 12-month horizon relative to a baseline. Both companies incorporate assumptions regarding balance sheet composition, prepayment behavior, and deposit repricing (deposit betas). JPM describes its scenarios including parallel, steepening, and flattening shifts, while GS specifically quantifies its parallel shocks as 100- and 200-basis point moves. Both explicitly state that these scenarios exclude responsive management actions.

sentences.text: Earnings-at-risk scenarios estimate the potential change to a baseline over the following 12 months utilizing multiple assumptions.

These scenarios include a parallel shift involving changes to both short-term and long-term rates by an equal amount; a steeper yield curve involving holding short-term rates constant and increasing long-term rates; and a flatter yield curve involving increasing short-term rates and holding long-term rates constant or holding short-term rates constant and decreasing long-term rates.
• The impact on exposures as a result of instantaneous changes in interest rates from baseline rates.
We measure EaR over a one-year time horizon following a 100- and 200-basis point instantaneous parallel shock in both short- and long-term interest rates.

These scenarios include contractual elements of assets, liabilities, preferred stock, and certain off-balance sheet instruments, such as rates of interest, principal repayment schedules, maturity and reset dates, and any interest rate ceilings or floors, as well as assumptions with respect to our balance sheet size and composition, prepayment behavior and deposit repricing.

Deposit repricing is captured by evaluating the change in deposit rate paid relative to the change in market rates (deposit beta) and we calibrate the deposit betas used in our models by using a number of factors, including observed historical behavior, future expectations, funding needs and the competitive landscape.

comparisons.peer_topic: Wealth Management Net Interest Income Sensitivity Analysis Methodology and Assumptions
comparisons.peer_summary: The analysis evaluates the impact of instantaneous parallel interest rate shocks on the Wealth Management segment's net interest income over the next 12 months, incorporating forecasts of balance sheet activity, prepayment behavior, reinvestment, and deposit pricing sensitivity. The model assumes no management action in response to scenarios and excludes changes in correlated macroeconomic variables, reflecting subjective assumptions about customer and market re-pricing behavior.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley analyze the impact of instantaneous parallel interest rate shocks on net interest income over the next 12 months. Both methodologies incorporate forecasts of balance sheet activity, prepayment behavior, reinvestment, and deposit pricing sensitivity. Crucially, both disclosures explicitly state that the sensitivity analysis assumes no management actions are taken in response to the rate shocks. JPM identifies parallel, steepening, and flattening shifts, while MS focuses on parallel shocks with a floor in downward scenarios.

sentences.text: Earnings-at-risk scenarios estimate the potential change to a baseline over the following 12 months utilizing multiple assumptions.

These scenarios include a parallel shift involving changes to both short-term and long-term rates by an equal amount; a steeper yield curve involving holding short-term rates constant and increasing long-term rates; and a flatter yield curve involving increasing short-term rates and holding long-term rates constant or holding short-term rates constant and decreasing long-term rates.
• The impact on exposures as a result of instantaneous changes in interest rates from baseline rates.

The previous table presents an analysis of selected instantaneous upward and downward parallel interest rate shocks (subject to a floor of zero percent in the downward scenario) on net interest income over the next 12 months for our Wealth Management business segment.
The forecast includes modeled prepayment behavior, reinvestment of net cash flows from maturing assets and liabilities, and deposit pricing sensitivity to interest rates.

The sensitivity analysis assumes that we take no action in response to these scenarios, assumes there are no changes in other macroeconomic variables normally correlated with changes in interest rates and includes subjective assumptions regarding customer and market re-pricing behavior and other factors.
